subject: Business
title: Stablecoins: Bridging Crypto and Fiat
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Stablecoins: Bridging Crypto and Fiat.

hook.text: Bitcoin swings 10% in a day. You can't price a cup of coffee in something that changes value every hour.

buildup.text: Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies pegged to stable assets like the US dollar, aiming for price stability.

discovery.text: Tether (USDT) processes more daily volume than Bitcoin and Ethereum combined. Stability has huge demand.

twist.text: Not all stablecoins are truly stable. TerraUSD collapsed in 2022, wiping out $40 billion in days.

climax.text: Regulators are racing to classify stablecoins. Are they currencies, securities, or something entirely new?

punchline.text: Stable in name doesn't mean stable in nature.

quiz.question: What happened to TerraUSD in 2022?
options: It lost its peg and collapsed, wiping out $40 billion
It became the world's most used stablecoin
It was adopted as legal tender in El Salvador

details.summary: Stablecoins are cryptocurrencies pegged to stable assets like the US dollar, combining blockchain technology with price stability. Tether and USDC maintain a one-to-one dollar peg through asset reserves, enabling fast global transfers without traditional cryptocurrency volatility.
details.whyItMatters: Stablecoins solve crypto's volatility problem for everyday payments and trading. They have become essential infrastructure for cryptocurrency markets and are increasingly used for international remittances and decentralized finance.
takeaways: Stablecoins maintain a fixed peg to fiat currencies like the US dollar
Reserves of cash, bonds, or algorithms maintain the price peg
They enable fast, cheap global transfers without cryptocurrency volatility

faq.question: How do stablecoins maintain their dollar peg?
faq.answer: Asset-backed stablecoins like USDC hold dollar reserves equal to coins in circulation. Holders can redeem tokens for dollars, creating arbitrage that maintains the peg. Algorithmic stablecoins use smart contracts to expand or contract supply, though these have proven less reliable.

faq.question: What went wrong with the TerraUSD stablecoin collapse?
faq.answer: TerraUSD relied on an algorithmic mechanism linked to a sister token Luna rather than actual dollar reserves. When confidence broke in May 2022, a death spiral destroyed both tokens, wiping out 40 billion dollars and demonstrating the risks of unbacked stablecoin designs.
